summary: Every convertible test runs on a controlled clock via db.now(), and the hygiene guard's exemption set holds only the reviewed class-3 spin-waits and class-4 kernel/subprocess stamps, each with its reason recorded beside the code.

children.title: One shared clock fixture for tests, seeded from a constant epoch
children.description: Four later work orders wait on your merge, so stay small. Do NOT migrate the four other ad-hoc patchers — _Clock and _MovedNow in tests/test_health_sweep.py, _rewind in tests/test_parked_work.py, the clock fixture in tests/test_evolution_report.py. A sibling owns those three files. tests/test_scheduler.py is your end-to-end proof, not a migration project: one site, one fixture. You are the only work order permitted to edit src/jarvis/testing.py, and every sibling is told to report an insufficient fixture rather than extend it — so the four modes have to be right here.
children.acceptance: tests/test_clock_fixture.py asserts all six properties in section 1 against literals and passes; tests/test_scheduler.py passes with its local _Clock deleted; tests/test_isolation_gate.py still passes. Mutation check quoted in the PR: seeding the fixture from time.time() makes the constant-epoch test fail. No file under src/jarvis/ except testing.py is modified, and the knowledge entry's kn-id is in the PR body.

children.title: Record class 3 and class 4 on the guard's exemption surface
children.spec_section: 2 — The exemption mechanism, and the two exempt classes
children.description: You change no production code under src/jarvis/ and convert nothing that is exempt. You do NOT own tests/test_health_sweep.py or tests/test_feature_validation.py even though both carry class-3 spin-waits: two siblings own those files and mark their own sites, because no test file belongs to two work orders. You ARE the only work order that may touch the mechanism, including widening the reason regex to admit class 4 — a sibling waits on that spelling and must not coin a second. Six siblings delete entries from the shape you settle, in parallel, so never end a turn with it half-converted.
children.acceptance: Every exempt site carries a file-specific reason, and the PR quotes the time.monotonic() or time.sleep( line each class-3 mark sits on — a mark with no spin-wait on the quoted line is wrong. `rg -o -N 'clock-exempt:.*' tests/ | sort | uniq -d` prints nothing. The ten pure class-3 files show a comment-only diff. The reason check accepts class 4 and still refuses class 2, with a test for each. Non-exempt sites in your files are converted. Targeted tests for all 15 files pass.

children.title: Migrate the four hand-rolled clocks onto the shared fixture

children.acceptance: _Clock, the clock fixture, _MovedNow and _rewind are gone and nothing re-implements them; no `jarvis.db.now =` direct assignment survives; no advance() caller passes minutes. Both mutations in section 3 are quoted in the PR: frozen-instead-of-ticking makes a STALE_FINISH_BLOCKER test fail, and advance(1) makes the first-look tests fail. children.title: Convert bulk fixture stamp construction to db.now()

If you find yourself needing to, the site belongs to a sibling — report it instead of reaching across. tests/test_uncollected_task_block.py looks like it belongs to you and does not: its sites are class 4 and another work order owns that file. You have no dependency and start at once: a sibling lands a shared clock fixture in src/jarvis/testing.py, and you must neither use it nor edit that file.
children.acceptance: The token-only diff command in section 4.1 prints nothing — every changed line differs from main only in the clock call. `git diff --name-only origin/main | rg '^src/'` prints nothing, and so does `git diff origin/main -- tests/ | rg '^\+.*clock'`. The residual-site scan over all ten files prints nothing. Targeted tests pass with per-file collected counts unchanged.

children.title: Convert display ages, log windows and the release staging marker
children.spec_section: 7 — Display ages, logs, and release staging
children.description: src/jarvis/uilog.py's five lines are one unit and so are src/jarvis/wiring.py's four: converting a subset of either is worse than converting none, and your section says why. Leave src/jarvis/release.py:264 and ui/app.py:348/:470 alone and add the comment saying why — they are exempt, not overlooked. Your src/jarvis/daemon.py lines (:5209 and the base-health sites near :7051) are thousands of lines from any sibling's, so do not range outside them. Two siblings have already merged: do not edit src/jarvis/testing.py, and reuse the merged class-4 reason spelling rather than coining one.
children.acceptance: rg over src/jarvis/uilog.py and src/jarvis/wiring.py for time.time() and time.localtime() prints nothing — both files move as a unit. A new frozen-clock boundary test proves a row at cutoff-1s is excluded and cutoff+1s included, and the section 7.1 mutation (writer reverted, reader converted) makes it go red, quoted in the PR. release.py:264 and ui/app.py:348/:470 unchanged with comments. tests/test_release_staging.py:593 and :606 carry a class-4 mark quoting the shell `date +%s` they compare against, and its 13 other sites are converted. Targeted tests pass under all three TZ settings.

justification: Seven children, under the cap of eight. Six were possible but would have put the shared clock fixture in the same work order as the 2300-line test file whose every clock.advance() caller it rewrites — and four children wait on that fixture's merge, so the gating child had to be the smallest, not the largest. The remaining six are cut by production surface so that no two touch one file: invariants.py and ops.py have a single owner, and daemon.py's three clusters are thousands of lines apart. Fewer children would mean one worker owning both src/jarvis/invariants.py and src/jarvis/uilog.py, which are unrelated subjects with unrelated false-green risks.
